tasks.subject: Task 1: Rust `get_list` command and list-page tests
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `get_list(kind)` returns a `SearchPage` for `airing`, `rating` or `clicks`, reusing the search parser.

**Files:**
- Modify: `src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`
- Create: `crates/proxer-parse/tests/lists.rs`
- Existing fixtures (already committed): `fixtures/list-airing.html`, `fixtures/list-rating.html`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `parse_search_page(list-airing.html)` returns 50 hits with unique ids, includes id 53 titled "One Piece", and `has_next` is true; the rating fixture the same, with the first hit's rating `Some(9.64)`.
- [ ] `list_path("airing") == Some("/anime/airing")`, `list_path("rating") == Some("/anime/animeseries/rating/all")`, `list_path("clicks") == Some("/anime/animeseries/clicks/all")`, anything else is `None`.
- [ ] The `get_list` command returns `Err("Unsupported")` for an unknown kind without any request, and is registered in `generate_handler!`.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes (50 + the new tests, 0 ignored).

**Verify:** `cargo test --workspace` → all pass

Full steps in the plan document, Task 1.

tasks.subject: Task 2: Design tokens, cover helper, API additions, demo
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `theme.css` tokens, `coverUrl`/language helpers with tests, `api.getList`, and a dev-only demo API so every screen can be rendered without logging in.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/theme.css`, `src/lib/ui/helpers.ts`, `src/lib/ui/helpers.test.ts`, `src/lib/demo.ts`
- Modify: `src/main.ts`, `src/lib/api.ts`, `src/App.svelte` (only the `<style>` block moves out)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `coverUrl(53) === "https://cdn.proxer.me/cover/53.jpg"`.
- [ ] `languagesOf(episodes)` returns the languages present across the episodes ordered engsub, engdub, gersub, gerdub, then any others alphabetically; `episodesWith(episodes, lang)` returns the episode numbers that have that language, ascending.
- [ ] `src/theme.css` defines the tokens (colors, spacing, radius, poster size, hero height, ring) and the `html.tv` and breakpoint overrides; it is imported in `main.ts`; the old global CSS in `App.svelte` is removed from there (behavior kept in `theme.css`: tv sizing, coarse-pointer 44px, focus ring).
- [ ] `api.getList(kind)` calls `get_list`; in a plain browser during `npm run dev` (no `window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__`) `api` is the demo API; a production build contains no demo data (verify with `grep -c "Dragon Ball Super" dist/assets/*.js` → 0).
- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run check` (0/0) and `npm run build` pass.

**Verify:** `npm test && npm run check && npm run build && grep -c "Dragon Ball Super" dist/assets/*.js` → tests pass, 0 errors, `0`

tasks.subject: Task 4: Shell, Home, and the restructured App
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A top-bar shell, the Home screen with rows, and `App.svelte` routing Login, Home, Search and Title through the shell.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/lib/ui/Shell.svelte`, `src/lib/Home.svelte`
- Modify: `src/App.svelte`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `Shell` shows a top bar (Proxer, tabs Home and Search with `aria-current="page"` on the active one, Log out) and a main area.
- [ ] `Home` loads `getList` for `airing`, `rating` and `clicks` in parallel; each row independently shows loading, ready, error (with retry) or is hidden when empty; the hero is the first hit of the airing list with an "Open" button.
- [ ] `NotLoggedIn` from any list returns to Login via `onauth`.
- [ ] After login the app starts on Home; tabs switch Home and Search; opening a poster opens the Title screen (Task 5; until then `Info` stays wired for the title screen so the app keeps working); Back from a title returns to the screen it came from.
- [ ] Dev only (`import.meta.env.DEV`): `?screen=home|search|title&id=N` starts on that screen (used for screenshots), ignored in production.
- [ ] `npm run check` (0/0), `npm run build` pass; screenshots in Task 6 show Home.

**Verify:** `npm run check && npm run build` → exit 0

tasks.subject: Task 5: Search grid, Title page with episode picker, Pla
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Search results as a cover grid, the Title page (hero, drawn action buttons, language chips, episode page chips, tiles, streams below), and the player restyled.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/lib/Title.svelte`, `src/lib/ui/EpisodePicker.svelte`
- Modify: `src/lib/Search.svelte`, `src/lib/Player.svelte` (styles only), `src/App.svelte` (use `Title` instead of `Info`)
- Delete: `src/lib/Info.svelte`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `Search` shows the search form in a bar and results in `PosterGrid`; paging (Previous/Next) and the stale/error handling behave as before.
- [ ] `Title` shows `Hero` with title, meta (Status and Genre from the info fields) and buttons: `▶ Watch` (primary, plays the first supported stream of the first episode in the selected language), then `Note`, `Favorite`, `Finished`, `Watchlist: this ep.`, `Watchlist: next ep.` as `disabled` buttons with `title="Available in the next update"`.
- [ ] `EpisodePicker` renders, left to right on one wrapped row: the "Episodes" label, language chips (from `languagesOf`), then page chips (only when more than one page, labels like "1 - 50"); below it the tiles for episodes having the chosen language; below the tiles the streams for the picked episode (button per stream with a Normal/Airing/Unsupported badge, Unsupported disabled) or "No streams (yet)". Picking a language keeps the picked episode if it has that language.
- [ ] Opening the player keeps the behavior of the old `Info`: stale-result guards for episode and stream loading, `Player` mounted inside the title screen via `{#key}`, Back from the title returns to the previous screen, Back closes the player first.
- [ ] `Player.svelte` logic is unchanged (diff limited to its `<style>` block and class names/wrappers); the toolbar uses the shared button styles.
- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run check` (0/0) and `npm run build` pass.

**Verify:** `npm test && npm run check && npm run build` → exit 0

Full steps in the plan document, Task 5.

tasks.description:
**Goal:** See every screen rendered at desktop, phone and TV sizes through the demo mode, fix layout problems found, and write the manual verification checklist for devices.

- Create: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-new-ui-manual-verification.md`
- Modify: any file under `src/` for fixes found

- [ ] With `npm run dev` running, headless Chrome screenshots exist for these 9 combinations and were looked at (Read tool): screens home, search (use `?screen=search`), title (`?screen=title&id=45`) at desktop 1280x800, phone 390x844, and TV 1920x1080 with `?tv=1`.
